note: Layering and core objects. Stack resolved by Spike 01: Electron shell (D17), CodeMirror 6 surface (D16). Full failure analysis has not been run; threats listed are those visible from decisions and spike findings.

layers.name: Features and UI
layers.description: Editor surface, section nav, search and filtered views, range operations. Consumes X.

layers.name: Logical objects
layers.description: Natural domain objects exposing conceptual operations; translate them into the language of W.

layers.name: Infrastructure
layers.description: Files on disk, directory watching, atomic replacement, OS services, and from v2 the network hub.

components.name: Editor surface
components.description: CodeMirror 6. Vim is a switchable setting (D15); the non-vim keymap is first-class and is what mobile always runs. Inline widgets in a viewport ViewPlugin, block widgets in an incrementally-updated StateField; constructs unrender under the cursor and blocks unrender from a neighbouring line. Binds to a DocumentWindow, which is the complete editor-facing API (D26, renamed in D35); reaches Document only for undo, which is document-scoped.

components.name: Section nav
components.description: Sections as expandos; the default section holds pins.

components.name: Search and filtered views
components.description: One filtered-view mechanism over tag, date and text queries.

components.name: Range operations
components.description: Select a range, then tag, bookmark, print or branch it.

components.name: Document
components.description: One logical markdown document: text and inferred spans (dates, headings, anchors, tags). Owns history and durability. Positions are (segment, offset); the stream’s segments are dates.
components.storage: Segmented into day files for the stream; a single file for branched documents and pinned lists.

components.name: Corpus
components.description: The set of documents; enumeration; anchor resolution by name.
components.storage: Opens documents by name. Does not scan the directory directly.

components.name: Fileset
components.description: Ordered typed entries: bookmark, file, URL, external document.

components.name: FilesetCollection
components.description: Iteration over all filesets; updating a reference globally across them.

components.name: Search
components.description: One query mechanism over tags, dates and text, returning ranges.
components.storage: v1 scans through the Document API; later maintains an index fed by Document change events.

components.name: Range
components.description: A transient selection and the operations on it. A persisted range is inline markup, never offsets.

components.name: Local directory
components.description: Plain files at a stable, user-visible path. A replica for text, a cache for attachments.

components.name: Directory watcher
components.description: Watches directories, never file descriptors.

components.name: OS services
components.description: Electron main process. Printing (range rendered to HTML in the web layer, with an explicit base href), clipboard and image paste, open-with by OS intent.

components.name: Derived index
components.description: Machine-local, never synced, disposable, never authoritative. Owned by Search; needs a startup consistency check with full rebuild on disagreement.

components.name: Sync client
components.description: Continuous asynchronous push; offline accumulation; divergence surfaced with a picker.

components.name: Network hub
components.description: Single source of truth. The only component outside the user's physical control.

components.name: Electron shell
components.description: Serves the app from a custom scheme registered with registerSchemesAsPrivileged({secure:true}). Not file://, not a localhost server.

components.name: Write-ahead log
components.description: .tephra/wal — changes since the last file write. Seconds long, discarded on write. Explicitly NOT a history (D32).

components.name: History
components.description: Versions of the corpus: commit, versions, read, restore(version, doc, span?). The only durable history. Commit on ~5min quiescence or every 30min or session end; never blocks typing.

components.name: Git repository
components.description: notebook/.git, gitignoring .tephra/. Local in v1; gains a remote at v2a. Chosen over a bespoke store because it extends the exit to the history.

components.name: Pane (view-model)
components.description: Navigation and extent policy: location, back stack, boundary state, ExtentPolicy. Consumes Document/Region/Corpus. The editor reports viewportChanged; the Pane decides whether to extend. ui-state.json is this, serialised.

flows.label: read text through the X API (never a W-level scan)
change events; Document stays ignorant of consumers
notifies; History decides when to commit
viewportChanged — reports a fact, does not decide
goTo / extend — opens and replaces Regions

trust_boundaries.description: Everything except the hub runs on a trusted device. The hub is outside the user's physical control and holds third-party information found in the notes.

threats.name: Silent loss when divergent copies reconcile
threats.rationale: 'Losing anything, ever' is an explicit unacceptability criterion.
threats.mitigation: Divergence surfaced with a picker, never resolved silently (D12).

threats.name: Interrupted write corrupts a day file
threats.rationale: Autosave makes partial writes the ordinary risk rather than the exotic one.

threats.name: Cache eviction discards text not yet pushed
threats.rationale: Between an offline write and its push, the local copy is the only copy.
threats.mitigation: Text is a replica and never evictable; only attachments are cached (D5).

threats.name: Watcher dies silently on atomic replace
threats.rationale: It stops firing without erroring, so the editor and disk drift apart unreported.

threats.name: Hub compromise exposes third-party information
threats.rationale: Notes discuss people who did not consent to the hub.
threats.mitigation: Open — bears on where the hub lives (Q2).

threats.name: Credential leakage; Android TLS trust unresolved
threats.rationale: Portal's one unclosed spike hole, inherited: a vendored OpenSSL has no trust anchors and Android's store uses legacy hashed filenames.

threats.name: A stale derived index is trusted
threats.rationale: Hand-editing is a feature, so index staleness is routine rather than exceptional.
threats.mitigation: Index is machine-local, disposable and never authoritative (D7); startup consistency check with full rebuild on disagreement.

threats.name: A local HTTP server inside the app is reachable by any other local process
threats.rationale: The corpus holds other people’s information, so a localhost origin is a real exposure rather than a theoretical one.
threats.mitigation: Avoided by design: custom scheme, no port, no listener (D17). Do not substitute a dev server for convenience.

threats.name: The vim keymap implementation ignores CodeMirror atomic ranges
threats.rationale: Two of D16’s three design constraints exist to work around a third-party gap; if the package is abandoned or fixed, behaviour shifts underneath.
threats.mitigation: The workaround — unrender under the cursor — is arguably correct behaviour independently of the bug.

threats.name: Deleted text survives forever in version history
threats.rationale: With a git repository from v1 (D32), deleted content persists indefinitely rather than for 30 days — and from v2a it is also on the hub, which holds other people’s information.
threats.mitigation: Inherent to having history at all. Purging is a history rewrite and, after v2a, a force-push: a documented procedure, NOT a button. The earlier "a purge clears the journal" mitigation is void.
